#318 CONTENTS. withLoadedKey(presence, directory, use): directory must exist as 0700 (never created), sealed blobs present and exactly 0600 (never repaired), then createPrimary and tpm2_load -C primary -u pub -r priv -c key.ctx -Q under the SAME primary, in a per-call mkdtemp 0700 scratch removed on return or throw (unseals run concurrently, so no shared context file). New Tpm2Reason key_not_sealed. N6 (fixture per-tool output and input flag tables, exit 3 on a missing input). The #316 reviewer's non-blocking N1-N4 folded in (fsync source-shape test via import.meta.dir with fsyncDirectory inside the publish loop; fsyncDirectory errors directory_unusable and the another-writer hint only on EEXIST; sealKey caller contract: setup lock held, a throw means not sealed). N5 (a lone private blob needs a named doctor/status state) is on WCLI-21 for slice 3. TSS2_LOG asserted absent from the child env; a failing load is tool_failed and stderr is never surfaced. NOT in #318: the salted session, tpm2_sessionconfig, the unseal itself, flush.

UNSEAL SESSION STEP IS BLOCKED ON A MEASUREMENT, then build it. Whether a session saved by tpm2_startauthsession survives into a SEPARATE tpm2_unseal process under /dev/tpmrm0 is unmeasured (docs and kernel source point both ways: the man page says most RMs flush sessions on disconnect and the saved-session approach does not work outside tpm2-abrmd; kernel tpm2-space.c gives each fd its own session table flushed on close; a mailing-list thread says a saved session outlives its process). I sent the leader the exact operator command list for jetson (createprimary with the pinned template, create, load, getcap handles-saved-session before and after, startauthsession --hmac-session -c primary.ctx -S s.ctx, sessionconfig, unseal -p session:s.ctx, cmp, flush); the leader routes it to the operator through opum-doc. It also settles that real tpm2-tools accepts -G ecc256:aes128cfb with the pinned -a set and -i -. IF it holds: per unseal, in the scratch: createPrimary, load, startauthsession --hmac-session -c primary.ctx -S s.ctx (FRESH each unseal, s.ctx asserted 0600 before unseal reads it), tpm2_sessionconfig must report encrypt AND decrypt (the AC2 stop; pass/fail in tests and T26), tpm2_unseal -c key.ctx -p session:s.ctx with the 32 bytes read directly from stdout, stderr never surfaced, tpm2_flushcontext of the session in a finally. IF it does NOT hold: AC2 says stop and return to opum-doc; the A/B to send through the leader is (A, my recommendation) libtss2-esys via bun:ffi, one connection for startauthsession and unseal, or (B) tpm2-abrmd TCTI, which changes the tpmrm0-only rule. Do not choose; do not improvise.

DEC-262 RULINGS BINDING (recorded verbatim as notes on WCLI-21 or WCLI-164): a9 design (key on pipes only, 0600 blobs in the 0700 dir, no PCR binding, the 32-byte key itself sealed, unseal in a salted HMAC session); a10 tool-trust walk; a11 symlink hops owner-only, tool_untrusted name accepted; a12 built env (PATH = tool dir + /usr/bin + /bin all walked, no LD_/DYLD_/HOME/parent PATH) and shebang interpreter walked; a13 a script interpreter is refused, not followed; a14 after env the rest of the line is one bare command name, env detected by written OR final basename. Design choices that are mine to record in the slice 3 ADR (WCLI-21): the primary template (-C o -g sha256 -G ecc256:aes128cfb -a restricted|decrypt|fixedtpm|fixedparent|sensitivedataorigin|userwithauth|noda) and sealed-object attributes (fixedtpm|fixedparent|noda|userwithauth), noda with empty userauth, tpm2_clear or an owner password makes the blob unloadable (named state and recovery), same-uid access (accepted by ADR 0001/0002), the ELF RUNPATH residual and the two env/wrapper residuals (all on WCLI-21 notes).

WCLI-21 SEQUENCE FROM HERE. 2b part 2b-2: the session step and unseal (after the measurement). Then slice 3 (KeyProvider and backend selection replacing the 7 createKeychainKeyProvider sites in src/cli/main.ts, reporting.ts states, the WCLI-21 ADR naming DEC-262, ADR 0004 Linux amendment, mapping EVERY Tpm2Reason including platform_unsupported, tool_untrusted, tool_output_too_large, tool_timeout, directory_unusable, tpm_unusable, key_not_sealed, tool_failed to contract codes and doctor states, plus a state for a lone private blob and for blobs unloadable after tpm2_clear), slice 4 (T26 harness and runbook; jetson run includes an operator reboot; ask the leader; NO BINARY GOES TO JETSON BEFORE SLICE 4), slice 5 (advertise Linux after T26; may touch the release path: stop and report before committing). NO REAL KEY IS PIPED anywhere until the unseal slice is reviewed. Each PR at most about 400 lines; tell the leader early if one will pass it. Send the leader the fence (paths, tests, dependencies) and wait for CLEAR before the first commit of a slice; if a DEC-182 (1) path class or a dependency is needed, stop and report before committing.

ENVIRONMENT AND METHOD. Prefix Bash calls with: export PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.2/bin:$PATH; (DEC-266). Run git push, gh pr merge and git merge each BARE in its own call (a composed or piped command is refused; a hook refuses a push joined to anything, and judges a composed command whole, so git checkout -b X && git commit is refused as a commit on dev: branch first in its own call). A hook rejects shell-variable write targets in cp/sed -i and redirects: use literal paths (a for-loop with sed -i on a variable also fails). The classifier refused a gh pr close of my own PR; do not close or reopen PRs: to re-run CI push one empty commit (the Check job was once never created on a head; the empty commit fixed it). quest writes: --actor ward-cli-worker --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse; quest task complete moves the record to .quest/completed/, so git add -A .quest/; a task must be In Progress before complete; pass long verbatim notes with a quoted heredoc to a scratchpad file and --add-note "$(cat file)". Tracker-only PRs land the usual way: branch off dev, one commit, push, PR, wait for all three checks (poll gh api actions runs jobs by the full commit SHA; gh pr checks reports an empty window right after a push), merge bare with --match-head-commit. Mutation checks are part of the proof: mutate the CHECK, confirm the predicted subset goes red, restore byte-for-byte (cp from a scratchpad copy and cmp), and make sure the mutation line really matched (a biome-reformatted line made one sed a no-op and read green). Run biome format --write on own files only. Fake tpm2 tools generate a 0660 file for each output flag, and Bun chmodSync drops the sticky bit (use chmod(1)). Reasoning rules from the leader: ask before a PR goes far past about 400 lines; wait for the leader's floor on a PR when it says it will re-run one; questions only the operator can answer go to the leader as an A/B choice with the recommendation first; never merge or promote without the leader's word; report to the leader before stopping or blocking.
